visaReferences.description: Known for its affordable cost of living and beautiful Adriatic coast, Albania's"Unique Permit" is a very accessible option for remote workers.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign company.
Minimum annual income of ~$10,000 (~$820/month).
Proof of accommodation and health insurance.
Clean criminal record.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Digital nomads on the visa are exempt from Albanian income tax on foreign-sourced income.

visaReferences.description: The Nomad Digital Residence (NDR) program allows remote workers to live in a Caribbean paradise. The visa is valid for up to two years.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a non-local company.
Annual income of at least $50,000 USD (~$4,167/month).
Health insurance coverage.
Clean criminal record.

visaReferences.description: Argentina's visa allows nomads to stay for 180 days, renewable for another 180. It offers access to Buenos Aires' extensive cultural and culinary life.
requirements: Work remotely for a foreign company.
Demonstrate sufficient funds (no fixed minimum is published).
Available to nationals of visa-waiver countries.
Valid passport and clean criminal record.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Exempt from Argentine income tax for up to 12 months under the digital nomad visa.

visaReferences.description: Armenia offers a very accessible path by allowing remote workers to register as sole proprietors. The country has a simple, low-tax system. No minimum income is stated.
requirements: Obtain a residency permit by registering as a self-employed person.
No minimum income requirement to register.
Open a local bank account.
Provide an address in Armenia.

visaReferences.description: Aruba's"One Happy Workation" program allows a stay of up to 90 days. While not a long-term visa, it's an attractive option for short stays.
requirements: Hold a passport from an eligible country (e.g., US).
Proof of remote work for a non-Aruban company.
Sufficient funds to support the stay (no specific amount).

visaReferences.description: The Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay (BEATS) program allows professionals and students to work or study remotely from the islands for up to one year.
requirements: Valid passport.
Proof of remote work or student status.
Sufficient funds to support yourself during your stay.
No specific minimum income is required.

visaReferences.description: The"Barbados Welcome Stamp" allows remote workers to live on the island for 12 months, with an option to renew. It's one of the most popular Caribbean programs.
requirements: Proof of remote employment or self-employment.
Annual income of at least $50,000 USD (~$4,167/month).
Health insurance valid in Barbados.
visaReferences.taxNotes: No Barbadian income tax on remote earnings during the Welcome Stamp period.

visaReferences.description: Belize's"Work Where You Vacation" program (Long Stay Visitor Permit) allows a stay of up to 6 months, aimed at professionals who want to enjoy the country's natural beauty.
requirements: Citizen or permanent resident of the EU, UK, USA, or Canada.
Proof of employment with a foreign company.
Annual income of at least $75,000 USD for individuals (~$6,250/month), or $100,000 with dependents.
Health insurance with at least $50,000 USD coverage.

visaReferences.description: The"Work From Bermuda" certificate allows remote workers to live in this self-governing British territory for one year. No minimum income is specified, but the cost of living is high.
requirements: Proof of remote employment or enrollment in higher education.
Sufficient funds to support your stay.
Health insurance and a clean criminal record.

visaReferences.description: Brazil's digital nomad visa allows for an initial stay of one year, renewable for another year. The income requirement is one of the most reasonable.
requirements: Proof of remote work status.
Monthly income of at least $1,500 USD from foreign sources, OR a bank balance of at least $18,000.
Clean criminal record and health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: You become a tax resident in Brazil after 183 days of physical presence, which triggers taxes on global income.

visaReferences.description: Bulgaria offers a Type D Visa through a freelance permit. It boasts a low cost of living, a growing tech scene in Sofia, and a 10% flat tax rate.
requirements: Obtain a freelance permit from the Employment Agency.
Prove sufficient financial means (no fixed amount is published).
Non-EU/EEA national.
Bulgaria is a full Schengen member since January 2025 (air/sea borders opened March 2024).
visaReferences.taxNotes: Flat income tax rate of 10%, one of the lowest in the EU.

visaReferences.description: The Cabo Verde Remote Working Program allows a stay of six months, renewable for another six. It targets remote workers from Europe, North America, and ECOWAS countries. Note: the program portal has been offline - verify availability before applying.
requirements: Proof of remote work and sufficient funds.
Average bank balance of at least €1,500 (~$1,630 USD) over the last 6 months.
Valid passport and travel insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Remote workers are exempt from local income taxes on foreign-sourced income.

visaReferences.description: While there is no specific nomad visa, Cambodia's E-Class Business Visa is a popular long-term option for remote workers. It is extendable for up to one year.
requirements: Initially a 30-day visa, extendable for 1, 3, 6, or 12 months.
No official income requirements.
Requires obtaining a Cambodian work permit to work legally.

visaReferences.description: Colombia offers a digital nomad visa (V-Nómadas Digitales) valid for up to two years. The income requirement is based on 3x the Colombian monthly minimum wage.
requirements: Passport from a visa-exempt country.
Proof of remote work for a foreign company.
Monthly income of at least 3x SMMLV (COP 5,252,715 in 2026, ~$1,200 USD) for each of the last 3 months.
Health insurance with coverage in Colombia.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Nomads are subject to Colombian tax after 183 days; foreign income might be taxed if tax residency is triggered.

visaReferences.description: Costa Rica's"Estancia por Teletrabajo" visa is for one year, extendable for a second. Nomads are exempt from income tax and can enjoy the"Pura Vida" lifestyle.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign entity.
Stable monthly income of at least $3,000 USD ($5,000 for families).
Health insurance covering the duration of the stay.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Exempt from Costa Rican income taxes on all foreign-sourced remote income.

visaReferences.description: Croatia offers a temporary residence permit for nomads, granting up to 18 months (shorter grants can be extended once). It's known for its beautiful coastline.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign company.
Monthly income of at least €3,622.50 (2.5x the average Croatian net salary, recalculated annually).
Proof of accommodation and health insurance.
Clean criminal record check.
visaReferences.taxNotes: 100% tax-exempt on remote income generated outside of Croatia.

visaReferences.description: The @HOME in Curaçao program allows remote workers to stay on the island for up to six months, with a possible six-month extension.
requirements: Proof of remote work or ability to support oneself financially.
No specific minimum income is listed.
Valid passport and health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Remote income earned from outside Curaçao is not subject to local income tax.

visaReferences.description: Cyprus attracts nomads with its sunny weather and strategic location. The permit is for one year, renewable for two more. You are not subject to local income tax.
requirements: Proof of remote work for clients or an employer outside Cyprus.
Net monthly income of at least €3,500 (~$3,800 USD).
Proof of accommodation and health insurance.
Clean criminal record.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Non-domicile tax residents enjoy exemptions on dividend and interest income in Cyprus.

visaReferences.description: The Czech Republic offers a long-term visa for business (Zivno), popular among freelancers. It requires a trade license and proof of funds rather than a monthly income.
requirements: A trade license (Zivnostenske opravneni)
Proof of funds of CZK 156,500 (~$6,800 USD, 50x the subsistence minimum) - not a monthly income test
Proof of accommodation and a clean criminal record
Extensions are limited to the first year; longer stays require switching to a residence permit
visaReferences.taxNotes: Subject to Czech flat tax rate of 15% on income; lump-sum expense deductions available for freelancers.

visaReferences.description: Dominica's"Work in Nature" (WIN) visa allows a stay of up to 18 months, targeting professionals who want to work surrounded by the island's lush nature.
requirements: Proof of remote work.
Expected annual income of $50,000 USD (~$4,167/month).
Health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: No income tax on foreign-sourced remote earnings in Dominica.

visaReferences.description: Ecuador offers a professional, technical, or artisanal visa (Rentista) for up to two years. It's a great option for those seeking adventure in a biodiverse country.
requirements: Proof of a stable income from foreign sources.
Minimum monthly income of three unified basic salaries ($1,410 USD, based on the 2025 SBU of $470).
Clean criminal record and health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Foreign-sourced income is not subject to Ecuadorian income tax for digital nomad visa holders.

visaReferences.description: Estonia was a pioneer, launching one of the first dedicated digital nomad visas. It allows you to work remotely for a company registered abroad for up to one year.
requirements: Proof of remote work contract or business registration.
Monthly income of at least €3,960 (~$4,300 USD, calculated as €132 per day) for the last 6 months.
Health insurance for Estonia.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Estonian tax residency is triggered after 183 days of stay; standard flat rate of 20% applies.

visaReferences.description: Georgia's"Remotely from Georgia" program allows citizens of 95 countries to stay and work for at least 180 days and up to a year. It's known for its simple application and low cost of living.
requirements: Citizen of one of the 95 eligible countries.
Proof of remote work.
Monthly income of at least $2,000 USD.
Travel health insurance for the entire stay.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Foreign-sourced income is tax-free in Georgia; only locally-sourced income is taxed at 20%.

visaReferences.description: Germany offers a freelance residence permit (Aufenthaltserlaubnis, §21 AufenthG) allowing self-employed remote workers to live in the country for up to 3 years. There is no fixed minimum income; viability of your freelance activity is assessed case-by-case.
requirements: Evidence the freelance activity is economically viable (clients, contracts, financing).
Applicants under 45 must show adequate pension provision.
German health insurance and registered address (Anmeldung).
visaReferences.taxNotes: Subject to German income tax as a tax resident; progressive rates up to 45%.

visaReferences.description: Greece's digital nomad visa offers a two-year stay with a potential for extension and a 50% tax break for up to 7 years, providing access to a beautiful Mediterranean lifestyle.
requirements: Work remotely for a foreign employer or your own foreign-registered company.
Net monthly income of €3,500 (~$3,800 USD).
Clean criminal record and health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: 50% tax cut on income earned in Greece for up to 7 years (requires commitment to stay).

visaReferences.description: Grenada's Remote Employment Act of 2021 allows a one-year stay, renewable for another year. It caters to those looking for a quiet Caribbean work-life balance.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a non-Grenadian company.
Annual income of at least $37,000 USD (~$3,083/month).
Valid passport and health insurance.

visaReferences.description: Hungary's"White Card" is a residence permit for digital nomads. It allows a stay of one year, extendable for one more. It targets high-income remote workers.
requirements: Proof of remote work contract outside of Hungary.
Monthly income of at least €3,000 (~$3,250 USD) for the last 6 months.
Cannot have shares in a Hungarian company.
Proof of accommodation.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Hungarian tax residency triggers after 183 days, subject to a flat 15% income tax rate.

visaReferences.description: Iceland offers a long-term visa for remote workers with a very high income requirement. It's for high-earning professionals looking to experience Iceland's unique nature.
requirements: Must not be an EU/EEA/EFTA citizen.
Proof of remote work for a foreign company.
Monthly income of 1,000,000 ISK (approx. $7,200 USD).
Health insurance valid in Iceland.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Exempt from Icelandic tax if you stay less than 183 days (the maximum duration of the visa anyway).

visaReferences.description: Indonesia's E33G Remote Worker KITAS allows digital nomads to live in Bali and beyond for up to one year. A shorter B211A Visit Visa (up to 180 days) is also available with lower requirements.
requirements: E33G KITAS: Annual income of at least $60,000 USD ($5,000/month).
B211A Visit Visa: Proof of $2,000 USD in savings (up to 180 days).
Proof of employment or business ownership outside Indonesia.
Valid passport with at least 6 months validity.
Proof of health insurance and clean criminal record.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Remote workers are exempt from Indonesian income taxes on foreign source income under specific conditions.

visaReferences.description: Ireland does not have a dedicated nomad visa. The Atypical Working Scheme allows short-term (max 90 days) specialized assignments arranged by a host employer. Longer stays require a standard employment permit.
requirements: A host company in Ireland must arrange the Atypical Working Scheme application.
Salary must meet the General Employment Permit threshold (EUR 34,000/year).
The 90-day cap applies with a cooling-off period before reuse.

visaReferences.description: Launched in 2024, Italy's Digital Nomad Visa targets "highly skilled" professionals. It grants a one-year renewable permit.
requirements: Must be a"highly skilled worker" (degree or 3+ years experience).
Minimum annual income of €28,000 (~€2,333/month, ~$2,680 USD).
Health insurance covering all risks in Italy.
Proof of accommodation.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Income tax flat reductions (up to 70-90% exemption under local tax schemes for relocated workers).

visaReferences.description: Japan introduced a digital nomad visa in 2024 for citizens of 49 countries that have tax treaties with Japan. It allows a stay of up to six months but cannot be renewed (6-month wait before reapplying).
requirements: Citizen of a visa-exempt country with a tax treaty with Japan (49 eligible countries)
Annual income of at least ¥10 million (~$68,000 USD)
Private health/travel insurance with at least ¥10 million in treatment coverage
Proof of remote work or freelance activity
visaReferences.taxNotes: Remote income is tax-exempt for the 6-month duration of the stay.

visaReferences.description: Kazakhstan's "Neo Nomad Visa" (Category B12-1) launched in November 2024. It targets remote workers earning foreign income, offering a low-tax stay with no obligation to file local taxes on overseas earnings.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign employer or clients.
Monthly income of at least $3,000 USD (6 months of bank statements).
Tax return from country of citizenship.
Criminal record certificate (apostilled).
Health insurance valid in Kazakhstan for the full visa period.
No local employment permitted.

visaReferences.description: Kenya's Class N "Digital Nomads" permit (not to be confused with Class K for retirees) allows remote workers employed by foreign companies to live in Kenya. No specific income threshold is published on the official portal: only proof of foreign income via bank statements.
requirements: Work for an employer or clients outside Kenya (local employment prohibited).
Bank statements or payslips for the last 3 months proving foreign income.
Employer/company cover letter to the Director General.
Valid passport and proof of accommodation.
Issuance fee: USD 1,000/year. Processing fee: USD 200.

visaReferences.description: Latvia offers a temporary residence permit for remote workers, allowing stays of up to one year with renewal while conditions hold.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign employer.
Monthly income of at least 3x the Latvian minimum monthly wage (€2,340/month as of April 2026).
Valid health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Micro-enterprise tax of 25% on turnover up to €25,000; standard progressive rates above.

visaReferences.visaLength: 3-12 months, renewable up to 24 months total
visaReferences.description: The DE Rantau Nomad Pass aims to establish Malaysia as a leading digital nomad hub. It is issued as a Professional Visit Pass of 3-12 months, renewable once.
requirements: Proof of remote work (freelancer or remote employee).
Annual income of at least $24,000 USD ($2,000/month) for tech talent, or $60,000 USD for non-tech talent.
Spouses may not work locally.
Valid passport and health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Remote income generated outside of Malaysia is tax-exempt.

visaReferences.visaLength: 1 year, renewable up to 3 times (max 4 years)
visaReferences.description: Malta's Nomad Residence Permit is for non-EU nationals and allows a stay of one year. Malta offers an English-speaking environment and sunny Mediterranean climate.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign company.
Gross annual income of at least €42,000 (~€3,500/month) for applications since April 2024.
Valid travel document and health insurance (EU + UK coverage).
Rental or purchase agreement for accommodation.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Remote income is not taxed in Malta unless it is remitted or spent locally.

visaReferences.description: The Mauritius Premium Visa is a free, one-year renewable visa for remote workers. It offers a tropical lifestyle with no local income tax obligations.
requirements: Proof of remote work and funds from outside Mauritius.
No minimum income requirement.
Must not enter the Mauritian labour market.
Proof of accommodation and health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Flat 15% tax rate, but foreign-sourced income is not taxed if earned outside Mauritius.

visaReferences.description: Mexico's Temporary Resident Visa is very popular with remote workers. It allows stays longer than 180 days and up to four years.
requirements: Proof of economic solvency.
A monthly income of at least 300x the daily UMA (MXN 35,193/month in 2026, ~$1,850 USD), OR equivalent savings.
Must be applied for from a Mexican consulate outside of Mexico.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Foreign source income is not taxed in Mexico as long as you do not trigger local business/employment operations.

visaReferences.description: Montenegro offers a temporary residence permit for digital nomads, allowing a stay of up to two years, with a possible extension of another two.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign company (or your own company not registered in Montenegro).
Proof of sufficient financial means (no fixed amount is published).
Proof of accommodation.
Valid travel document and health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Flat personal income tax rate of 9-15% depending on income; foreign income may be exempt if not a tax resident.
visaReferences.referenceIncome: No fixed minimum (proof of remote work required)

visaReferences.visaLength: Up to 2 years (full re-application required on renewal)
visaReferences.description: Moldova's Digital Nomad program is technically a temporary residence permit, not a visa. Launched September 2025, the income requirement is formula-based (18× the current year's forecasted average monthly salary) rather than a fixed dollar amount.
requirements: Remote work exclusively for a foreign-registered legal entity (employment, service, or shareholder contract).
Show income of 18× the current-year forecasted average monthly salary over the preceding 6 months (~$3,022/month for 2026).
Criminal record certificate (apostilled, waived on renewal).
Valid health insurance in Moldova.
Proof of accommodation.
In-person application at the General Inspectorate for Migration (GIM).

visaReferences.description: Morocco does not have a specific digital nomad visa. However, remote workers can enter on a standard tourist visa for up to 90 days.
requirements: Sufficient funds to support your stay.
Stays under 183 days are exempt from local income tax.

visaReferences.description: Namibia launched a digital nomad visa in 2022, allowing a stay of up to six months. Ideal for those wanting to explore the country's unique landscapes.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign employer.
Minimum monthly income of $2,000.
Health insurance and clean criminal record.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Foreign-sourced income is not taxed in Namibia for digital nomad visa holders.

visaReferences.description: The Netherlands has no digital nomad visa. The closest routes are the self-employed residence permit (points-based business plan assessment) and the Dutch-American Friendship Treaty (DAFT) for US entrepreneurs.
requirements: Self-employed route: a business plan scored on viability via RVO points system.
DAFT route (US citizens only): investment capital in a Dutch business, not an income threshold.
No remote-work-for-foreign-employer category exists.

visaReferences.visaLength: Up to 9 months per visitor visa
visaReferences.description: New Zealand introduced a remote work allowance for visitor visa and NZeTA holders in January 2025. This is not a dedicated digital nomad visa; remote work is simply permitted under existing visitor visa conditions. Work must be for overseas employers only.
requirements: Hold a valid visitor visa or NZeTA (applied for on or after 27 January 2025).
Work must be for an overseas employer or client: no work for NZ employers.
Sufficient funds for the duration of stay (standard visitor visa requirement).
92-day tax threshold: NZ tax may apply if staying 92+ days in a 12-month period.

visaReferences.description: North Macedonia announced a digital nomad permit in 2024, but it was never enacted. Remote workers use ordinary temporary residence routes under the Law on Foreigners.
requirements: Details are yet to be announced (TBA).
Expected to offer low living costs.

visaReferences.visaLength: Up to 2 years per grant (self-employed route)
visaReferences.description: Norway has no digital nomad visa. The former independent contractor permit has been discontinued. The closest route is a self-employed permit requiring a company abroad and skilled-worker qualifications.
requirements: An assignment contract with one Norwegian enterprise (not remote work for foreign clients).
Pay not poorer than normal in Norway: at least NOK 545,400/year (~$4,500/month, bachelor level).
Skilled-worker qualifications required.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Svalbard has no income tax; mainland Norway has progressive rates from 22-47.4%.

visaReferences.description: Panama's Short-Stay Visa for Remote Workers is valid for nine months and renewable once. It offers a low cost of living and a strategic location.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign company.
Annual income of at least $36,000 USD ($3,000/month).
Health insurance valid in Panama.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Panama uses a territorial tax system. Foreign-sourced income is completely tax-free.

visaReferences.description: Paraguay has no dedicated digital nomad visa, but foreign nationals can apply for temporary residency under general categories (Ley 6984/22), making it an option for remote workers. The process involves submitting documents and obtaining a residence permit.
requirements: Proof of economic solvency (no specific amount).
Clean criminal record.
Birth and marriage certificates.

visaReferences.description: Peru launched the "nomada digital" residence category with a one-year duration (renewable) for remote workers.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a company outside Peru.
Minimum monthly income of $1,240 USD.
Health insurance.

visaReferences.description: The Philippines' Digital Nomad Visa, launched via Executive Order No. 86, allows a stay of up to 12 months with a 12-month extension. Applicants must be from a country that offers a reciprocal visa to Filipino nationals.
requirements: Minimum annual income of $24,000 USD (~$2,000/month).
Must be a citizen of a country offering reciprocal nomad visa to Filipinos.
Proof of remote work or freelance contracts with foreign clients.
Health insurance and clean criminal record.

visaReferences.description: Poland doesn't have a dedicated nomad visa, but non-EU freelancers and remote workers can obtain a temporary residence permit via Voivodeship offices.
requirements: Proof of stable and regular income (no fixed minimum; subsistence benchmark ~PLN 776/month).
Health insurance.
Proof of accommodation.

visaReferences.visaLength: 4-month visa, then 2-year permits up to 5 years
visaReferences.description: Portugal's D8 visa is highly popular. It offers a path to residency and access to the Schengen Area. The country boasts a great quality of life and active startup and engineering hubs in Lisbon and Porto.
requirements: Proof of income from remote work.
Monthly income of at least 4 times the Portuguese minimum wage (€3,480/month in 2025, ~$4,000 USD; revised annually).
Proof of accommodation for at least 12 months.
Clean criminal record and private health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Non-Habitual Resident (NHR) scheme is closed for new entries; standard progressive tax rates apply (up to 48%).

visaReferences.description: As a US territory, Puerto Rico requires no visa or time limit for US citizens. For others, a standard US visa (like ESTA for eligible countries) allows a 90-day stay.
requirements: US Citizens can work freely.
Others require a valid US visa (e.g., ESTA).
Tax incentives under Act 60 are available for residents.

visaReferences.description: Romania provides a digital nomad visa with one of the highest income requirements. It allows a one-year stay, which can be extended.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a company registered outside Romania.
Monthly income of at least three times the Romanian average gross salary (~€5,400/month as of 2025, ~$6,200 USD; floating target revised quarterly).
Income proven for each of the last 6 months.
Proof of accommodation and health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Romania does not tax foreign remote income if you remain a tax resident of another country.

visaReferences.description: The"Live It" program in Saint Lucia offers a multiple-entry visa for up to one year. It is aimed at individuals who want to work remotely while enjoying the island.
requirements: Proof of remote work and sufficient funds for the stay.
No specific minimum income is stated.
Valid passport.

visaReferences.description: Serbia's Law on Foreigners (amended February 2024) explicitly allows temporary residence for foreigners working remotely for foreign employers.
requirements: Proof of remote work and a reported monthly income of at least €3,500 (~$4,025 USD).
Low cost of living compared to the high income requirement.
Temporary residence is granted for up to 1-3 years depending on basis.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Flat income tax of 10% for residents; digital nomads may be exempt on foreign-sourced income if not a tax resident.

visaReferences.description: The Seychelles Workcation Program allows visitors to stay and work remotely for up to one year. It requires proof of being a remote worker or business owner.
requirements: Valid passport and proof of remote work/business ownership.
Proof of funds/income.
Health and travel insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Foreign-sourced remote income is not subject to Seychelles income tax.
visaReferences.referenceIncome: No minimum income (proof of remote work required)

visaReferences.description: South Africa has introduced a digital nomad visa (Immigration Amendment Act 2024), allowing remote work for a foreign employer.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign employer; may not serve the South African market
Annual earnings of at least R650,000 (~$34,000 USD or ~$2,900/month)
Sufficient funds and comprehensive health insurance
Clean criminal record
visaReferences.taxNotes: Exempt from South African income tax for the first 36 months if registered as a remote worker from a foreign employer.

visaReferences.visaLength: Up to 3 years (F-1-D, permanent since July 2026)
visaReferences.description: South Korea's F-1-D"workcation" visa was made permanent in July 2026 with eased eligibility and longer stays. The original 2024 pilot required high income and capped stays at 2 years.
requirements: Proof of remote work for a foreign company for at least 1 year.
Income threshold (originally KRW 85M/year ~ $5,500/month; lowered under the July 2026 rules, especially for applicants under 55).
Private health insurance enrollment required.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Income from foreign sources is generally not taxed in South Korea during the workation period.

visaReferences.description: Spain's digital nomad visa allows non-EU citizens to live and work remotely for up to five years. It offers a favorable tax regime under"Beckham's Law" (24% flat tax rate on Spanish-source income).
requirements: Proof of being a qualified professional (university degree or 3+ years of experience).
Work contract with a foreign company (active for at least 3 months).
Income of at least 200% of the Spanish minimum wage (€2,760/month in 2025, ~$3,100 USD).
Clean criminal record and comprehensive health insurance.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Eligible for "Beckhams Law" (reduced flat tax of 24% on income up to €600,000).

visaReferences.description: Sri Lanka officially launched its Digital Nomad Visa in February 2026. It allows remote workers to stay for 12 months, renewable annually. The visa fee is $500 USD.
requirements: Minimum monthly income of $2,000 USD from foreign sources.
Proof of remote work, freelancing, or business ownership outside Sri Lanka.
Valid passport (6+ months), health insurance, and clean criminal record.
Application fee of $500 USD.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Remote income from foreign sources is not taxed in Sri Lanka under the digital nomad visa.

visaReferences.description: Taiwan launched a Digital Nomad Visitor Visa in January 2025. The Employment Gold Card (open work permit + residence, 1-3 years) remains an option for highly skilled professionals.
requirements: Age 30+: annual salary of at least $40,000 USD in one of the last 2 years (age 20-29: $20,000/year).
OR hold another country's digital nomad visa.
Bank balance averaging at least $10,000 USD/month over the past 6 months.
Health insurance and proof of remote employment.
visaReferences.taxNotes: First 3 years: 50% tax exemption on salary income over NTD 3M; standard progressive rates (5-40%) apply after.

visaReferences.description: Thailand offers the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) for digital nomads and remote workers. It is a 5-year multiple-entry visa with 180-day stays per entry, extendable once.
requirements: Proof of remote work, freelancing, or being a digital nomad
Bank balance of at least 500,000 THB (~$14,000 USD) - a funds test, not an income test
Valid passport and health insurance
visaReferences.taxNotes: Taxation applies only to income brought into Thailand during the same tax year; foreign income is generally tax-free.

visaReferences.description: Turkey introduced digital nomad provisions in April 2024, implemented as a short-term residence permit for remote workers from designated countries. It offers a low cost of living and is tax-free for stays under 183 days.
requirements: Citizen of an eligible country (US, Canada, UK, EU, etc.).
Reported minimum monthly income of $3,000 USD.
Valid passport and proof of accommodation.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Remote income earned outside Turkey is generally not taxed if you stay under 183 days; otherwise progressive rates apply.

visaReferences.description: Dubai's virtual work program allows professionals to live in the emirate while working for companies overseas. It offers a tax-free environment and a high-tech lifestyle.
requirements: Passport with minimum 6 months validity.
Proof of employment with a contract valid for one year.
Monthly salary of at least $3,500 USD.
Health insurance with UAE coverage.
visaReferences.taxNotes: Zero personal income tax in the UAE on all remote and foreign-sourced income.

visaReferences.description: Uruguay offers the "Hoja de Identidad Provisoria - Nomada Digital" for six months, renewable. It's notable for not having a specific income requirement, though applicants must prove they can support themselves.
requirements: A sworn statement declaring you have the means to support yourself.
No specified minimum income.
Clean criminal record.
Offers a path to permanent residency.

visaReferences.description: Vietnam does not have a specific nomad visa, but its Tourist e-Visa is popular with remote workers, allowing stays of up to 90 days. It can be renewed by leaving and re-entering.
requirements: Tourist e-Visa available to citizens of most countries.
No official income requirement.
Low cost of living and large remote worker community.

visaReferences.description: Andorra offers a remote worker residency permit under its Digital Economy Law. It is set in a safe, low-tax European microstate with beautiful Pyrenean nature.
requirements: Work remotely for an employer or clients based outside Andorra.
Proof of monthly income of at least 3x Andorran minimum wage (approx. €4,128/month, ~$4,500 USD).
Proof of local accommodation (rental or purchase agreement).
Clean criminal record and private health insurance.

visaReferences.visaLength: Initially 60 days, extendable up to 1 year (renewable)
visaReferences.description: Kyrgyzstan launched a dedicated "Digital Nomad" status for IT, creative, and digital professionals, offering a path to low-tax residency in Central Asia.
requirements: IT, digital design, or tech sector professional.
Proof of stable remote income (approx. $5,000 USD/year, ~$417/month).
Clean criminal record and valid passport.
Allows registration as an individual entrepreneur with local bank accounts.

visaReferences.description: Slovenia offers digital nomads access to Ljubljana's charming city life, Alpine scenery, and a strategic location in the heart of Europe with full Schengen access.
requirements: Valid passport
Proof of employment or freelance work for a foreign entity
Proof of monthly income meeting threshold
Health insurance valid in Slovenia
Proof of accommodation
visaReferences.taxNotes: Progressive income tax rates from 16-50%; non-residents taxed only on Slovenian-source income.

citizenship.scope: All 13 countries on the reviewed Henley citizenship list, plus Vanuatu, with official-source route classifications and statuses. Coverage includes defined investment programs, discretionary exceptional-contribution and merit routes, and Argentina's announced program with intake unverified. Numeric amounts are for one main applicant in the authority's published currency, excluding additional fees. Null amounts and currencies indicate no fixed or verified operative threshold; capital notes explain the distinction. Inclusion does not establish eligibility or guarantee citizenship.

programs.summary: Choose an Economic Diversification Fund contribution or a unit in an approved real estate project. Applications go through an authorised agent and due diligence.
programs.family: The EDF page lists USD 250,000 for the main applicant and up to three qualifying dependants. Eligibility conditions and additional fees apply; this directory uses the single-applicant threshold.

routes.name: Economic Diversification Fund
routes.capital: Non-refundable contribution.
routes.fees: USD 1,000 processing per application, USD 7,500 main-applicant due diligence, USD 500 naturalisation certificate per person and USD 1,000 per mandatory interview. Enhanced due diligence and bank charges may apply. Agent and passport costs are not included in this threshold.

routes.name: Approved real estate
routes.capital: Hold for three years from citizenship, or five years if reselling to another citizenship-by-investment applicant. Resale value is not guaranteed.
routes.fees: USD 75,000 government fee for the main applicant, plus processing, due diligence, naturalisation and interview fees. Enhanced due diligence and bank charges may apply. Purchase, agent and passport costs are outside the threshold.

sources.title: CBIU: Economic Diversification Fund
sources.supports: Active application route, contribution threshold, non-refundable nature, fees, family contribution and authorised-agent process.

sources.title: CBIU: Real Estate Investment
sources.supports: Approved-project threshold, holding periods and government and additional fees.

programs.summary: Contribute to the National Development Fund or purchase real estate in an approved project. A licensed local agent submits the application; property must normally be held for five years.
programs.presence: The official passport page requires five days in Antigua and Barbuda within the first five years after citizenship for passport renewal consideration.
programs.family: The NDF page allows a spouse, dependent children and dependent parents over 55 in the application. It lists USD 230,000 for a family of four or less, plus USD 20,000 processing and separate due diligence fees. Confirm qualifying dependants with the unit.

routes.name: National Development Fund
routes.capital: One-time contribution to the National Development Fund.
routes.fees: USD 10,000 processing, USD 8,500 main-applicant due diligence and USD 300 passport fee. Agent charges are additional.

routes.name: Approved real estate
routes.capital: Purchase in an approved project. Hold for five years unless replacing it with another officially approved property.
routes.fees: USD 10,000 processing, USD 8,500 main-applicant due diligence and USD 300 passport fee. Property transaction and agent costs are additional.

sources.title: CIU: National Development Fund
sources.supports: Active application route, contribution threshold, single and family processing fees, dependants and licensed-agent process.

sources.title: CIU: Antigua and Barbuda Passport
sources.supports: Five-day presence condition within the first five years for passport renewal consideration.

sources.title: CIU: Real Estate
sources.supports: USD 300,000 approved-project route, five-year holding period, replacement-property exception and processing fees.

sources.title: CIU: Schedule of Fees
sources.supports: USD 8,500 main-applicant due diligence, USD 300 passport fee and processing fees for NDF and real estate applications.

programs.summary: Property purchases, bank deposits and government bonds can qualify for exceptional citizenship, subject to the President's decision. These routes require a three-year holding commitment.

routes.name: Qualifying real estate
routes.capital: Title deed restriction prevents resale for at least three years. The authority also accepts equivalent foreign currency. Resale value is not guaranteed.
routes.fees: The investment-office page does not publish a complete fee schedule. Property registration, insurance, translation and professional costs are separate.

routes.name: Bank deposit
routes.capital: Deposit in a bank operating in Türkiye, with no withdrawal for at least three years. Equivalent foreign currency is accepted; the banking regulator must attest compliance.
routes.fees: The investment-office page does not publish application or bank charges.

routes.name: Government bonds
routes.capital: Purchase government bonds and retain them for at least three years. Equivalent foreign currency is accepted; the Ministry of Treasury and Finance must attest compliance.
routes.fees: The investment-office page does not publish application or bond transaction charges.

sources.title: Invest in Türkiye: Acquiring Property and Citizenship
sources.supports: Current property, bank-deposit and government-bond routes, USD 400,000 and USD 500,000 thresholds, three-year restrictions, equivalent foreign currency, regulatory attestations and presidential decision.

programs.summary: Choose a National Transformation Fund contribution or an investment in an approved project. The USD 270,000 property threshold applies to shared ownership of a qualifying tourism unit, with a separate government contribution.
programs.presence: IMA states that a visit to Grenada is not required before, during or after the application. The due-diligence process includes an online interview.
programs.family: The USD 235,000 NTF contribution covers the main applicant and up to three qualifying dependants, except siblings and parents or grandparents aged 55 or under, who attract additional contributions. Per-person fees also apply.

routes.name: National Transformation Fund
routes.capital: One-time donation to the National Transformation Fund, paid after approval.
routes.fees: USD 1,500 application and USD 1,500 processing for the main applicant. IMA's detailed table lists USD 5,000 due diligence plus USD 1,000 interview; its FAQ instead labels USD 6,000 as due diligence. The published fee breakdowns differ. Agent and passport costs are additional.

routes.name: Shared tourism real estate
routes.capital: Per applicant's share of a qualifying approved tourism-accommodation unit bought by two or more investors; developer-equity conditions apply. The five-year period from citizenship must elapse before resale to another CBI applicant. The general approved-project threshold is USD 350,000.
routes.fees: USD 50,000 government contribution, plus application, processing, due-diligence and interview charges listed for the NTF route. Property transaction and agent costs are additional.

sources.title: IMA Grenada: Becoming a Citizen
sources.supports: Active NTF and approved-project application routes, USD 235,000 contribution, family exclusions, detailed fee table, mandatory interview and authorised-agent process.

sources.title: IMA Grenada: Enquiries and FAQs
sources.supports: No visit requirement, online interview and the USD 6,000 due-diligence figure that differs from the detailed application table.

sources.title: Grenada: SRO 15 of 2024
sources.supports: NTF contribution and family additions, USD 350,000 general approved-project threshold and USD 50,000 government contribution.

sources.title: Grenada: SRO 21 of 2025
sources.supports: USD 270,000 per-share threshold for jointly purchased approved tourism units and developer-equity conditions; amendments concern developer fees, not applicant due-diligence fees.

sources.title: Grenada: Citizenship by Investment Amendment Act 3 of 2019
sources.supports: Section 5: five years from citizenship before disposal for resale to another applicant using the same approved real estate.

programs.summary: The Sustainable Island State Contribution funds government development priorities. The developer real estate route instead requires a unit in an approved development held for seven years. Applications go through an authorised agent and an interview.
programs.family: USD 250,000 covers a main applicant or a family of up to four under SISC. Each additional dependant costs USD 25,000 if under 18 or USD 50,000 if 18 or older. Due diligence is USD 7,500 for each dependant aged 16 or over.

routes.name: Sustainable Island State Contribution
routes.capital: Non-refundable contribution to the Federal Consolidated Fund after approval in principle.
routes.fees: USD 10,000 main-applicant due diligence and USD 250 application processing per person. Agent and passport costs are additional.

routes.name: Developer real estate
routes.capital: Purchase a designated unit in an approved development. Hold for at least seven years before resale.
routes.fees: USD 25,000 main-applicant post-approval fee, USD 10,000 due diligence and USD 250 application processing. Insurance fund contributions, conveyance, agent and passport costs are additional.

sources.title: CIU: Sustainable Island State Contribution
sources.supports: Active SISC route, USD 250,000 single or family threshold, additional dependant contributions, due diligence and interview requirements.

sources.title: CIU: Developer's Real Estate Investment
sources.supports: Current USD 325,000 approved-development threshold, seven-year holding period, post-approval and due-diligence fees and purchase costs.

sources.title: Saint Kitts and Nevis: SRO 20 of 2024
sources.supports: Regulation 21: non-refundable SISC contribution. Regulations 24 to 26: due diligence, USD 250 processing and post-approval fees. Current property threshold is sourced from the CIU's updated route page.

programs.summary: Contribute to the National Economic Fund or hold non-interest-bearing National Action Bonds for five years. The 2026 regulations also require a sworn declaration of at least USD 350,000 in financial resources.
programs.family: The USD 240,000 NEF contribution covers the main applicant and up to three qualifying dependants. Each additional dependant costs USD 10,000 if under 18 or USD 20,000 if above 18. The USD 300,000 bond investment covers any number of qualifying dependants; per-person fees are separate.

routes.name: National Economic Fund
routes.capital: Non-refundable contribution to the National Economic Fund after approval.
routes.fees: USD 2,000 main-applicant processing and USD 8,000 due diligence. An applicant interview and identity-verification process applies. Agent and passport costs are separate.

routes.name: National Action Bonds
routes.capital: Non-interest-bearing government bonds registered in the applicant's name and held for five years from first issue.
routes.fees: USD 50,000 non-refundable administration fee, plus USD 2,000 main-applicant processing and USD 8,000 due diligence. Agent and passport costs are separate.

sources.title: CIP Saint Lucia: Citizenship by Investment
sources.supports: Active NEF and National Action Bond routes, current investment thresholds, family contributions, five-year non-interest-bearing bonds, administration, processing and due-diligence fees.

sources.title: Saint Lucia: Citizenship by Investment Regulations SI 89 of 2015
sources.supports: Regulation 9: non-refundable NEF contribution. Regulation 12: five-year non-interest-bearing bond holding. Historical thresholds and superseded fees are not used.

sources.title: Saint Lucia: Gazette of 9 July 2024, SI 106
sources.supports: Operative USD 240,000 NEF threshold and additional dependant contributions, replacing older FAQ prices.

sources.title: Saint Lucia: Citizenship by Investment Amendment Regulations SI 57 of 2026
sources.supports: USD 8,000 main-applicant due diligence, USD 350,000 financial-resources declaration and biometric-data requirement. Also distinguishes new built-property rules from existing approved projects.

programs.summary: The Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Program, presented by the Naoero Program Office, uses a direct Treasury Fund contribution. A licensed agent submits the application, with due diligence and a principal-applicant interview.
programs.presence: No residence requirement. Interviews can be virtual or in person; applicants unable to take the oath in person may use an audiovisual link or an authorised oath-taker in another jurisdiction.
programs.family: A spouse and eligible children, parents and siblings can be included. The contribution schedule adds USD 2,000 per dependant aged 16 or over and USD 15,000 per sibling of the applicant or spouse. Application and due-diligence fees are separate.

routes.name: Treasury Fund contribution (regular amount)
routes.capital: Direct Treasury Fund contribution. The official August 2026 brochure lists USD 115,000 as the regular amount. A USD 90,000 offer is published for applications filed before 31 December 2026; that temporary amount is not used as the standing threshold.
routes.fees: USD 5,000 application, USD 6,000 principal-applicant due diligence, USD 1,200 bank due diligence and transaction charge, and USD 500 per passport. Agent advisory fees are additional.

sources.title: Naoero Program Office: Contribution
sources.supports: Active Treasury Fund route, USD 90,000 temporary contribution with 31 December 2026 deadline, dependant contributions and current application, due-diligence, bank and passport fees.

sources.title: Naoero Program Office: August 2026 Brochure
sources.supports: Pages 20 to 21 explicitly state USD 115,000 regular contribution, USD 90,000 limited offer ending 31 December 2026, and fee breakdown. No price is inferred from Henley's listing.

sources.title: Naoero Program Office: How to Apply
sources.supports: Licensed-agent submissions, due diligence, mandatory principal-applicant interview, Cabinet decision, oath arrangements and separate agent advisory fees.

sources.title: Naoero Program Office: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.supports: No residence requirement, remote interview and oath options, and eligible family categories.

programs.summary: Donate to the National Transformation Fund after approval in principle. Applications go through a licensed marketing agent, and the citizenship unit checks identity, background and source of funds.
programs.presence: The citizenship unit states that physical residence or relocation is not required during or after the application process.
programs.family: The fund donation is USD 95,000 for a family of two to four, plus USD 5,000 for each additional qualifying dependant. The unit lists spouses or de facto partners, children, parents and grandparents; eligibility and document fees apply.

routes.name: National Transformation Fund
routes.capital: Donation to the National Transformation Fund, completed after approval in principle.
routes.fees: USD 5,000 submission fee per application and USD 750 per applicant for the registration certificate, passport and national ID. A benefactor pays USD 5,000 due diligence if the application is sponsored. Agent costs are additional.

sources.title: São Tomé and Príncipe CIU: Donation to the National Transformation Fund
sources.supports: Active donation route, USD 90,000 single and USD 95,000 family contributions, additional dependants, submission and document fees, benefactor due diligence, family categories and no physical-residence requirement.

sources.title: São Tomé and Príncipe CIU: Application Process
sources.supports: Licensed-agent submission, background and source-of-funds checks, approval in principle and completion of donation before citizenship documentation.

programs.summary: Egypt offers a Treasury grant, property purchase, business investment with a grant, or a Central Bank deposit. The deposit is repaid in Egyptian pounds after three years without interest; the Prime Minister makes the citizenship decision.

routes.name: Treasury grant
routes.capital: Non-refundable grant to the Treasury, transferred from abroad. Instalments over up to one year are permitted; withdrawal or default before completion has separate refund rules in Egyptian pounds, without interest.
routes.fees: USD 10,000 non-refundable application fee, separate from the grant.

routes.name: Real estate purchase
routes.capital: Property purchase funded from abroad. Disposal within five years requires a separate USD 250,000 non-refundable Treasury payment to retain citizenship.
routes.fees: USD 10,000 non-refundable application fee. Property transaction costs are outside the investment threshold.

routes.name: Business investment and Treasury grant
routes.capital: USD 350,000 invested in a project plus a USD 100,000 non-refundable Treasury grant. Liquidation, closure or disposal of the investment within five years of operation requires a USD 250,000 Treasury payment to retain citizenship.
routes.fees: USD 10,000 non-refundable application fee, additional to both the business investment and the grant.

routes.name: Central Bank deposit
routes.capital: Transfer from abroad into a special Central Bank account. Repaid after three years in Egyptian pounds at the Central Bank exchange rate on repayment, without interest.
routes.fees: USD 10,000 non-refundable application fee, separate from the deposit.

sources.title: Egyptian Cabinet Citizenship Unit: Investment Programs
sources.supports: Four current routes, USD 250,000 grant, USD 300,000 property, USD 350,000 business plus USD 100,000 grant, USD 500,000 deposit, disposal conditions and repayment currency. Arabic official page read through a text-fetch proxy after direct connections timed out.

sources.title: Egyptian Cabinet Citizenship Unit: Application Steps
sources.supports: Current application process, USD 10,000 non-refundable application fee, investment completion and final Prime Minister decision. Arabic official page read through a text-fetch proxy.

programs.summary: Jordan's direct routes include qualifying existing businesses and newly issued company shares. The JOD 350,000 business threshold requires three years of qualifying assets and Jordanian employment outside the Capital Governorate.

routes.name: Existing business outside the Capital Governorate
routes.capital: Investor's average share of eligible fixed and non-current tangible assets over the last three audited years. Average Jordanian employment must be at least 10, with at least 90% of the required level maintained each month for those three years.
routes.fees: The Ministry of Investment's route page does not publish an application-fee schedule.

routes.name: Existing business within the Capital Governorate
routes.capital: Investor's average share of eligible fixed and non-current tangible assets over the last three audited years. Average Jordanian employment must be at least 20, with at least 90% of the required level maintained each month for those three years.
routes.fees: The Ministry of Investment's route page does not publish an application-fee schedule.

routes.name: Newly issued company shares
routes.capital: Purchase within four months of ministry approval through one licensed broker; no margin financing, pledging or lending. Each company's shares may comprise at most 10% of the required investment. Funds, including trading profits, cannot be withdrawn or disposed of for five years.
routes.fees: The Ministry of Investment's route page does not publish application or brokerage charges.

sources.title: Jordan Ministry of Investment: Jordanian Citizenship Through Investment
sources.supports: Active electronic applications; direct existing-business routes at JOD 350,000 or JOD 700,000 with three-year asset and employment tests; JOD 1,500,000 share route and five-year restrictions. Separate temporary-passport and residence routes are not included.

programs.summary: The Development Support Program accepts applications through designated agents. Its USD 130,000 single-applicant selling price is a programme payment, with Financial Intelligence Unit checks and Citizenship Commission approval.
programs.family: Published programme prices are USD 150,000 for a married couple, USD 165,000 with one child and USD 180,000 with two children. The fee table lists USD 10,000 for an additional applicant; qualifying dependant rules apply.

routes.name: Development Support Program
routes.capital: Minimum programme selling price under the DSP regulations, not a property or deposit investment. The 25% of the prescribed government fee paid before Commission consideration is non-refundable if the application is refused.
routes.fees: The current fee page lists USD 5,000 FIU due diligence and VUV 5,000 application fee. DSP regulations also prescribe VUV 10,000 per citizenship certificate. Passport charges are separate.

sources.title: Vanuatu Citizenship Office: Fees and Charges
sources.supports: Current USD 130,000 single-applicant and family price table, USD 5,000 FIU fee and VUV 5,000 application fee. The separate older Form D figures below the table are not treated as DSP prices.

sources.title: Vanuatu: Development Support Program Regulations, Order 33 of 2019
sources.supports: Clauses 4, 6 and 7: USD 130,000 DSP selling-price floor, designated-agent process, 25% government-fee non-refund rule on refusal and VUV 10,000 certificate fee. The older USD 2,000 due-diligence figure is superseded by the office's current fee table.

sources.title: Vanuatu Citizenship Office: FIU Due Diligence Checks
sources.supports: Ongoing operation of DSP, CIIP and VCP and the updated FIU submission process, supported by the linked 14 January 2025 notice.

programs.summary: Citizenship for exceptional services in Austria's special national interest is assessed case by case. Economic achievements can qualify, but the Interior Ministry expressly says that money transfers alone are insufficient.

routes.name: Citizenship for exceptional services
routes.capital: The ministry's criteria under section 10(6) of the Citizenship Act set no fixed investment threshold. Economic assessment considers business ownership or substantial influence, employment, completed investments or projects, and benefits to Austria. The federal government must confirm the special national interest.
routes.fees: The Interior Ministry's exceptional-services criteria do not publish an application-fee schedule.

sources.title: Austria Interior Ministry: Citizenship in the Special Interest of the Republic
sources.supports: Section 10(6) exceptional-services framework, federal-government confirmation, individual assessment, economic-achievement criteria and the express statement that money transfers alone are insufficient. No fixed investment amount or currency is specified.

programs.summary: Malta's merit route assesses exceptional services, contributions or national interest through a proposal, due diligence and a ministerial decision. The current regulations deleted the former direct-investment provisions in 2025.
programs.presence: After approval in principle, the naturalisation application must include proof of at least eight months of residence in Malta before the application date.

routes.name: Naturalisation on the basis of merit
routes.capital: No fixed investment threshold. The proposal describes the applicant's achievements, exceptional service or contribution, and plans to continue contributing after naturalisation. The formal application also requires adequate residential property, subject to the regulatory exceptions, and other ties to Malta.
routes.fees: The regulations provide for non-refundable administrative and other applicable fees set by the agency. The reviewed merit guide and regulations do not give a numeric fee schedule.

sources.title: Community Malta Agency: Citizenship by Naturalisation on the Basis of Merit
sources.supports: Current discretionary merit route under article 10(9), proposal and evaluation process, ministerial decision, eight-month residence requirement, residential property and individual contribution commitments. No fixed investment threshold is stated.

sources.title: Malta: Granting of Citizenship by Naturalisation on the Basis of Merit Regulations, SL 188.06
sources.supports: Regulations 5, 11A and 11B: merit criteria, proposal, due diligence, residence, property exceptions and agency-set fees. Legal Notice 159 of 2025 deleted the former direct-investment provisions in regulations 15 to 19 and the investment schedule.

programs.summary: Argentina has a legal framework for citizenship through relevant investment. The Economy Ministry announced contribution and bond options for Q4 2026; open intake has not been verified from the official sources reviewed.

routes.name: Announced citizenship-by-investment program
routes.capital: The Economy Ministry's 2 October 2026 announcement proposes a USD 350,000 non-refundable Treasury contribution or a USD 800,000 program-specific government bond. These are announced terms; a currently available qualifying investment threshold and bond holding or repayment terms have not been verified.
routes.fees: The official announcement does not publish application or due-diligence fees.

sources.title: Argentina Economy Ministry: Citizenship by Investment Program Announcement, 2 October 2026
sources.supports: Officially proposed USD 350,000 non-refundable contribution and USD 800,000 bond, due-diligence assessment and migration-authority decision. The announcement says intake will become operational during Q4 2026; it does not establish that applications are already open.

sources.title: Argentina Economy Ministry: Relevant Investments and Citizenship under Decree 524/2025
sources.supports: Official explanation of Decrees 366/2025 and 524/2025, the relevant-investment citizenship framework, the investment agency's assessment and recommendation, security checks and the migration authority's decision. This legal framework alone does not verify current intake.

remoteMarket.scope: Country-explicit fully remote listings passing verified-original-date age checks. Multi-country listings count once for each explicitly allowed country. Worldwide and unresolved location restrictions are excluded from country rankings. Employer headquarters are not used.
